nodes.name: MariaDB ColumnStore
nodes.gap: The proposed orange/downstream-only verdict is refuted on two independent grounds. First, "downstream-only" requires a distro to actually ship the package; live checks today (2026-09-04) confirm none does -- Ubuntu noble search returns zero hits, [Debian's tracker 404s](https://tracker.debian.org/pkg/mariadb-columnstore), and Arch Linux RISC-V has no entry -- so there is no downstream floor to apply and `release_provider` is correctly `none`, but the sub-type is wrong. Second, and more importantly, this is not merely "untested but buildable" (the bar for orange): live inspection of [MariaDB/server:storage/columnstore/CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/MariaDB/server/blob/main/storage/columnstore/CMakeLists.txt#L54-L56) confirms today that riscv64 is excluded from the `CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR` allowlist (build silently skipped), and even bypassing that guard, [datatypes/mcs_int128.h](https://github.com/mariadb-corporation/mariadb-columnstore-engine/blob/develop/datatypes/mcs_int128.h#L34-L46) unconditionally emits x86 SSE inline assembly (`movups`/`movdqu xmm0`) on any non-aarch64 GCC/Clang target, which is a confirmed ABI/assembler incompatibility on riscv64, not a hypothetical one; and even if that were patched, [primitives/primproc/archcheck.h](https://github.com/mariadb-corporation/mariadb-columnstore-engine/blob/main/primitives/primproc/archcheck.h) plus `primproc.cpp:711-713` contain a hard-coded runtime abort ("Unsupported CPU architecture. ARM Advanced SIMD or x86_64 SSE4.2 required; aborting.") for any architecture other than x86_64/aarch64 -- an explicit, in-code upstream statement that other architectures (including riscv64) are unsupported and will not run. Three independently confirmed, verified-live layers of breakage (config-skip, compile failure, guaranteed runtime abort) satisfy the skill's red bar ("known ABI incompatibility" and "explicit upstream statements that the architecture is unsupported"), which the orange verdict understated.

edges.note: The Debian/Ubuntu libpq5 binary package depends on libssl3 and libpq is built with OpenSSL-based SSL/TLS support ([Ubuntu libpq5 package](https://packages.ubuntu.com/jammy/libpq5), [libpq SSL Support docs](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/libpq-ssl.html)).

libpq is the C client library used to connect to and communicate with a PostgreSQL server, so it has no purpose without a PostgreSQL server to connect to ([libpq docs](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/libpq.html)).

Psycopg's [README](https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/blob/master/README.rst) states the pure-Python `psycopg` package "has only a runtime dependency on the libpq, the PostgreSQL client library, which should be installed in your system," and it is loaded at runtime (or linked directly by the optional C extension) to speak the PostgreSQL wire protocol.

Psycopg is a PostgreSQL database adapter for Python — per its [homepage](https://www.psycopg.org/) it exists solely to connect Python applications to a running PostgreSQL server, so it is useless without one available.

pgx is a Go client driver/toolkit for PostgreSQL that implements the wire protocol itself and requires a running PostgreSQL server to be useful, per the [pgx README](https://github.com/jackc/pgx) and [pkg.go.dev docs](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/jackc/pgx/v5).

pgjdbc is a pure-Java Type-4 driver that implements the PostgreSQL wire protocol and is only useful when connecting to a running PostgreSQL server, as stated in the [project README](https://github.com/pgjdbc/pgjdbc/blob/master/README.md) ("allows Java programs to connect to a PostgreSQL database... communicates in the PostgreSQL native network protocol").
PostgreSQL uses OpenSSL for TLS/SSL client-server connections, optional but enabled by default in production distro packages (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).
PostgreSQL optionally embeds CPython to support the PL/Python procedural language (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).
PostgreSQL requires glibc for its C runtime, math library (libm), and POSIX threading (pthreads) (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).
PostgreSQL optionally links LLVM to JIT-compile query execution, though this is disabled on riscv64 distro packages due to segfaults (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).
PostgreSQL optionally uses zlib for WAL and network compression, enabled by default (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).
PostgreSQL optionally uses ICU for Unicode collation and locale-aware text handling, enabled by default (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).
PostgreSQL optionally supports LZ4 compression for WAL and table (TOAST) data (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).
PostgreSQL optionally supports zstd compression for WAL and table data; the 4-way decompression loop is disabled on riscv64 ([zstd#4622](https://github.com/facebook/zstd/issues/4622)).
psql, PostgreSQL's interactive client, optionally links readline for interactive line editing, enabled by default (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).
PostgreSQL optionally links libxml2 to support the XML data type (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).
The contrib/xml2 module optionally links libxslt for XSLT transformations (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).
libpq-oauth optionally links libcurl to support OAuth authentication flows on Linux (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).
PostgreSQL optionally uses liburing for io_uring-based asynchronous I/O (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).
PostgreSQL optionally links libnuma for NUMA-aware memory allocation (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).
PostgreSQL optionally supports GSSAPI/Kerberos authentication (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).
PostgreSQL optionally supports PAM authentication (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).
PostgreSQL optionally supports LDAP authentication (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).
contrib/uuid-ossp optionally links a UUID library variant (bsd/e2fs/ossp) for UUID generation (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).
PostgreSQL requires Perl at build time for parser and catalog generation, with no runtime impact (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).
PostgreSQL requires flex and bison at build time for parser generation (project-reports/postgresql.md Section 9).

pgvector's own [META.json](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector/blob/master/META.json) declares a runtime prereq on PostgreSQL >= 13.0.0, and it builds as a loadable server extension via PGXS against `pg_config` (see the [Makefile](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector/blob/master/Makefile)), with no other package dependencies.

PostGIS is a spatial extension loaded into PostgreSQL, built against `postgresql-server-dev-all`/`postgresql-common` and packaged per PostgreSQL version (e.g. `postgresql-16-postgis-3`) per [Ubuntu packages.ubuntu.com](https://packages.ubuntu.com/source/noble/postgis) and the [PostGIS homepage](https://postgis.net/).
The Ubuntu `postgis` binary package runtime-depends on `libpq5`, the PostgreSQL C client library, per [packages.ubuntu.com](https://packages.ubuntu.com/noble/postgis).
The `postgis` source package build-depends on `libpcre2-dev` per [packages.ubuntu.com](https://packages.ubuntu.com/source/noble/postgis).

PostGIS's MVT (Mapbox Vector Tile) support build-depends on `libprotobuf-c-dev` and `protobuf-c-compiler`, the C bindings for Protocol Buffers, per [packages.ubuntu.com](https://packages.ubuntu.com/source/noble/postgis).
PostGIS's core geometry engine is provided by GEOS, built/linked via `libgeos-dev`/`libgeos-c1t64` per [packages.ubuntu.com](https://packages.ubuntu.com/source/noble/postgis).
PostGIS uses PROJ for cartographic reprojection, built/linked via `libproj-dev`/`libproj25` per [packages.ubuntu.com](https://packages.ubuntu.com/source/noble/postgis).
PostGIS raster support is built on GDAL, linked via `libgdal-dev`/`libgdal34t64` per [packages.ubuntu.com](https://packages.ubuntu.com/source/noble/postgis).

TimescaleDB is built and loaded as a PostgreSQL extension via PGXS/`pg_config` (its [CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/blob/main/CMakeLists.txt) fails with `FATAL_ERROR "Unable to find 'pg_config'"` if no PostgreSQL install is found) and is enabled inside a database with `CREATE EXTENSION timescaledb`.

TimescaleDB's [CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/blob/main/CMakeLists.txt) requires PostgreSQL to be built `--with-openssl` for full compatibility and explicitly links `find_package(OpenSSL)`/`OPENSSL_LIBRARIES` (required, version >= 1.0) on Windows/MSVC builds, with OpenSSL used for TLS in native multi-node/telemetry networking code.

Apache AGE is built and loaded as a PostgreSQL extension (via PGXS, `CREATE EXTENSION age`) and is described by its own repo as "an extension for PostgreSQL" ([apache/age README](https://github.com/apache/age)), making PostgreSQL both a build-time and runtime dependency.

Citus is packaged and built as a PostgreSQL extension (loaded via shared_preload_libraries and CREATE EXTENSION citus, built via PGXS/pg_config against a specific PostgreSQL version), per the [Citus README](https://github.com/citusdata/citus/blob/main/README.md) and its build system.

Citus's coordinator-to-worker communication is implemented directly on libpq-fe.h, included throughout its source tree (e.g. [remote_transaction.h](https://github.com/citusdata/citus/blob/main/src/include/distributed/remote_transaction.h), [subscription.c](https://github.com/citusdata/citus/blob/main/src/backend/distributed/commands/subscription.c)).

Citus's [configure.ac](https://github.com/citusdata/citus/blob/main/configure.ac) enables --with-lz4 by default and fails the build via AC_CHECK_LIB(lz4, LZ4_compress_default, ...) if the lz4 library/header is missing, used for columnar storage compression.

Citus's [configure.ac](https://github.com/citusdata/citus/blob/main/configure.ac) enables --with-zstd by default and fails the build via AC_CHECK_LIB(zstd, ZSTD_decompress, ...) if the zstd library/header is missing, used for columnar storage compression.

Patroni's [setup.py](https://github.com/patroni/patroni/blob/master/setup.py) declares psycopg2, psycopg2-binary, and psycopg[binary] (psycopg3) as extras used to connect to and control the managed PostgreSQL instance.
Patroni's [requirements.txt](https://github.com/patroni/patroni/blob/master/requirements.txt) lists `python-etcd` as the client library for its etcd Distributed Configuration Store (DCS) backend.

Patroni is described as a "PostgreSQL High-Availability orchestrator" ([setup.py](https://github.com/patroni/patroni/blob/master/setup.py)) that manages, bootstraps, and fails over an actual local PostgreSQL server process, so it is useless without a PostgreSQL installation to control.

Patroni's [patroni/dcs/kubernetes.py](https://github.com/patroni/patroni/blob/master/patroni/dcs/kubernetes.py) talks directly to the Kubernetes API (via urllib3, using in-cluster service-account credentials or a kubeconfig) to use Kubernetes endpoints/ConfigMaps as its DCS, so a running Kubernetes cluster is required when this backend is selected even though no pip package is declared for it.
PgBouncer's build requires [Libevent](https://github.com/pgbouncer/pgbouncer/blob/master/README.md) 2.0+ for its event loop, per the project README.
PgBouncer's build uses [OpenSSL](https://github.com/pgbouncer/pgbouncer/blob/master/README.md) 1.0.1+ for TLS support, per the project README and meson.build.
PgBouncer is a "[lightweight connection pooler for PostgreSQL](https://www.pgbouncer.org/)" and is useless without a PostgreSQL server to proxy connections to.

Pgpool-II is built against and links libpq (the Ubuntu `pgpool2` package depends on `libpq5`), and the [Pgpool-II install docs](https://www.pgpool.net/docs/latest/en/html/install-pgpool.html) require specifying the PostgreSQL client library path via `--with-pgsql`.

Pgpool-II can be built `--with-openssl` for TLS and AES256 password encryption, and the Ubuntu `pgpool2` package depends on `libssl3t64` ([packages.ubuntu.com](https://packages.ubuntu.com/noble/pgpool2), [install docs](https://www.pgpool.net/docs/latest/en/html/install-pgpool.html)).

Pgpool-II's in-memory query cache feature links against libmemcached (`--with-memcached`) and the Ubuntu `pgpool2` package depends on `libmemcached11t64` to talk to a Memcached server ([packages.ubuntu.com](https://packages.ubuntu.com/noble/pgpool2), [install docs](https://www.pgpool.net/docs/latest/en/html/install-pgpool.html)).

Pgpool-II is "middleware for PostgreSQL connection pooling, load balancing and high availability" that sits in front of PostgreSQL backend servers, so it is useless without PostgreSQL instances to pool/proxy ([pgpool.net](https://www.pgpool.net/mediawiki/index.php/Main_Page)).

pgcat is a "PostgreSQL pooler and proxy (like PgBouncer)" that sits in front of PostgreSQL primaries/replicas, so it has no purpose without a PostgreSQL backend to pool ([README](https://github.com/postgresml/pgcat)).

pgcat's [Cargo.toml](https://github.com/postgresml/pgcat/blob/main/Cargo.toml) pulls in the `jemallocator` crate on non-MSVC targets and `src/main.rs` sets `static GLOBAL: Jemalloc = Jemalloc;` as `#[global_allocator]`, statically linking jemalloc into the binary.

pgcat exposes a Prometheus statistics HTTP endpoint (a stable feature per the [README](https://github.com/postgresml/pgcat)), so it needs a Prometheus server to actually consume that data for monitoring to be useful.

CloudNativePG's go.mod requires k8s.io/client-go, k8s.io/api, k8s.io/apimachinery, and sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime, and the operator [directly integrates with the Kubernetes API server](https://cloudnative-pg.io/).
CloudNativePG is a Kubernetes operator (CRDs + controllers) and has no function outside a running Kubernetes cluster.
go.mod requires `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5 v5.10.0` as the Go PostgreSQL driver used by the operator's management/reconciliation code.
CloudNativePG exists solely to deploy, manage and orchestrate PostgreSQL clusters, [supporting primary/standby architecture using native streaming replication](https://cloudnative-pg.io/).

CNPG's Pooler CRD deploys and manages PgBouncer instances for connection pooling, implemented in the repo's dedicated `pkg/specs/pgbouncer` and `pkg/management/pgbouncer` packages (verified via GitHub code search).

CNPG links `prometheus/client_golang` and `prometheus-operator` API types to expose a [built-in exporter for Prometheus](https://cloudnative-pg.io/) and generate PodMonitor resources, which need a Prometheus (or compatible) server to scrape and be useful.

postgres-operator is a Kubernetes controller written against `k8s.io/client-go`, `k8s.io/api` and `k8s.io/apimachinery` (see [go.mod](https://github.com/zalando/postgres-operator/blob/master/go.mod)) and only functions by watching/managing Postgres CRDs and StatefulSets on a Kubernetes API server.

The operator's whole purpose is to provision and reconcile [PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/) clusters, connecting to them via the `github.com/lib/pq` driver in its Go code and, for logical backups, installing `postgresql-client-14..18` packages in [docker/logical-backup/Dockerfile](https://github.com/zalando/postgres-operator/blob/master/docker/logical-backup/Dockerfile).

The [README](https://github.com/zalando/postgres-operator#readme) states the operator delivers HA PostgreSQL clusters "powered by Patroni", and the operator ships a dedicated `pkg/util/patroni` client that calls each managed pod's Patroni REST API (`/switchover`, `/config`, `/restart`, `/cluster`) to perform failovers and config changes.

The operator builds and ships its own connection-pooler sidecar image by cloning and compiling [pgbouncer/pgbouncer](https://github.com/pgbouncer/pgbouncer) from source in [pooler/Dockerfile](https://github.com/zalando/postgres-operator/blob/master/pooler/Dockerfile), and the README lists "Database connection pooling with PGBouncer" as a feature.

The operator's Go module directly requires `github.com/lib/pq v1.12.3` (see [go.mod](https://github.com/zalando/postgres-operator/blob/master/go.mod)), which it uses to open SQL connections for role/database/extension management on the clusters it operates.

The operator's [go.mod](https://github.com/percona/percona-server-mysql-operator/blob/main/go.mod) directly requires `github.com/go-sql-driver/mysql` as the Go driver its controller code uses to connect to and manage MySQL instances.

The operator is built on `k8s.io/client-go`, `k8s.io/apimachinery` and `sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime` (per [go.mod](https://github.com/percona/percona-server-mysql-operator/blob/main/go.mod)) and only functions as a controller against a Kubernetes API server.

The operator's entire purpose is to deploy, scale and manage clusters of Percona Server for MySQL (images such as `main-psmysql8.4` in [deploy/cr.yaml](https://github.com/percona/percona-server-mysql-operator/blob/main/deploy/cr.yaml)), so it is useless without MySQL nodes to run.

The repo ships a Prometheus `ServiceMonitor` ([config/prometheus/monitor.yaml](https://github.com/percona/percona-server-mysql-operator/blob/main/config/prometheus/monitor.yaml)) so a Prometheus Operator can scrape the controller-manager's `/metrics` endpoint.
[Percona's install docs](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/pxc/helm.html) list Helm v3 as one of the two first-class ways (alongside kubectl) to install this operator.

[go.mod](https://github.com/percona/percona-server-mysql-operator/blob/main/go.mod) requires `github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager`, and controller code in `pkg/controller/ps/tls.go` integrates with it to issue and manage the cluster's TLS certificates.

postgres_exporter's [go.mod](https://github.com/prometheus-community/postgres_exporter/blob/master/go.mod) requires `github.com/lib/pq v1.12.3`, the pure-Go PostgreSQL wire-protocol driver it uses to open connections and run scrape queries.

The exporter is useless without a running PostgreSQL server to connect to via DATA_SOURCE_NAME/DATA_SOURCE_URI and scrape metrics from, as shown in the [README quick-start](https://github.com/prometheus-community/postgres_exporter#quick-start).

It is built to expose a /metrics endpoint in Prometheus exposition format for a Prometheus server's scrape_configs, per the [README example](https://github.com/prometheus-community/postgres_exporter#quick-start), which is its whole reason for existing.

MariaDB Connector/C's [CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/mariadb-corporation/mariadb-connector-c/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt) defaults `WITH_SSL` to `OPENSSL` on non-Windows builds, calling `FIND_PACKAGE(OpenSSL)` and linking `SSL_LIBRARIES`/`CRYPTO_LIBRARIES` to provide TLS support.; The [CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/mariadb-corporation/mariadb-connector-c/blob/3.4/CMakeLists.txt) offers OpenSSL (or GnuTLS) as the TLS/SSL backend for encrypted connections.

The operator provides "[Prometheus metrics](https://github.com/mariadb-operator/mariadb-operator/blob/main/docs/metrics.md) via [mysqld-exporter](https://github.com/prometheus/mysqld_exporter) and maxscale-exporter", deploying it as a sidecar ([README](https://github.com/mariadb-operator/mariadb-operator/blob/main/README.md)).

The operator has "Native integration with [prometheus-operator](https://github.com/prometheus-operator/prometheus-operator). Automatically create `ServiceMonitor` resources" and imports `prometheus-operator/prometheus-operator/pkg/apis/monitoring` in [go.mod](https://github.com/mariadb-operator/mariadb-operator/blob/main/go.mod), but the metrics it exposes are only useful once a running Prometheus scrapes them.

The operator declares `github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager v1.20.2` in [go.mod](https://github.com/mariadb-operator/mariadb-operator/blob/main/go.mod) and offers "Native integration with [cert-manager](https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager). Automatically create `Certificate` resources" for TLS ([README](https://github.com/mariadb-operator/mariadb-operator/blob/main/README.md)).

hiredis's optional `hiredis_ssl` target links `OpenSSL::SSL` when built with `ENABLE_SSL`, per [CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/redis/hiredis/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt), and Ubuntu's compiled `libhiredis1.1.0` package accordingly depends on `libssl3t64`.

hiredis is "a minimalistic C client library for the Redis database" per its [homepage](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/hiredis/) and needs a running Redis (or Redis-protocol-compatible) server to be useful.
jemalloc is bundled in `deps/` and used as Redis's default memory allocator on Linux, and builds on riscv64 per [jemalloc issue #2323](https://github.com/jemalloc/jemalloc/issues/2323).
OpenSSL is an optional dependency providing TLS transport when Redis is built with `BUILD_TLS=yes`.
Lua 5.1 is bundled in `deps/` as the scripting engine that powers Redis's `EVAL` command.
hiredis is bundled in `deps/` as the C client library used by `redis-cli` and Redis Sentinel.
xxHash is bundled in `deps/` and used for non-cryptographic hashing inside Redis.
HdrHistogram_c is bundled in `deps/` and used for latency percentile tracking.
linenoise is bundled in `deps/` to provide line-editing for `redis-cli`.
libsystemd is an optional runtime dependency used for systemd service notification support.

Valkey vendors jemalloc under [deps/jemalloc](https://github.com/valkey-io/valkey/tree/unstable/deps/jemalloc) and uses it as the default memory allocator on Linux, tuned via a custom `--with-lg-quantum=3` build option.

Valkey vendors a patched Lua 5.1 under [deps/lua](https://github.com/valkey-io/valkey/tree/unstable/deps/lua) to power `EVAL`/scripting, with local security and hashing modifications documented in [deps/README.md](https://github.com/valkey-io/valkey/blob/unstable/deps/README.md).
Valkey vendors LZ4 (v1.10.0) under [deps/lz4](https://github.com/valkey-io/valkey/tree/unstable/deps/lz4) for streaming compression support.

xxHash is bundled inside Valkey's vendored LZ4 sources ([deps/lz4/xxhash.c](https://github.com/valkey-io/valkey/tree/unstable/deps/lz4)) with symbols namespaced to avoid conflicts with loaded modules, per [deps/README.md](https://github.com/valkey-io/valkey/blob/unstable/deps/README.md).

Valkey links against OpenSSL (`USE_OPENSSL`, `OPENSSL_PREFIX`) in [src/Makefile](https://github.com/valkey-io/valkey/blob/unstable/src/Makefile) to provide optional TLS support for client and replication links.

KeyDB vendors [hiredis](https://github.com/Snapchat/KeyDB/tree/main/deps/hiredis) in `deps/` and links `libhiredis.a` (with `hiredis_ssl` when TLS is enabled) into the server build, per `src/Makefile`.

jemalloc is vendored in `deps/jemalloc` and is KeyDB's default memory allocator on non-ARM systems (`MALLOC=jemalloc`) per `src/Makefile` and the [README](https://github.com/Snapchat/KeyDB/blob/main/README.md).
Lua is vendored under `deps/lua` and built as a default dependency target for KeyDB's scripting engine (`EVAL`/`EVALSHA`), per `src/Makefile`.

KeyDB vendors RocksDB in `deps/rocksdb` and compiles `storage/rocksdb.o` when `ENABLE_ROCKSDB` is set, backing the experimental [FLASH storage](https://docs.keydb.dev/docs/flash) tiering feature described in the README.

KeyDB is built with TLS support via OpenSSL/libssl by default (`BUILD_TLS=yes`), linking against `libssl-dev`/OPENSSL_PREFIX per `src/Makefile` and the [README](https://github.com/Snapchat/KeyDB/blob/main/README.md).

Dragonfly's CMake build does `find_package(OpenSSL)` and links `OpenSSL::Crypto` into the core library for TLS support, per [CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/CMakeLists.txt) and [src/core/CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/src/core/CMakeLists.txt).

Dragonfly fetches and statically builds LZ4 1.10.0 as a third-party library, used by its RDB/snapshot compressor, per [src/external_libs.cmake](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/src/external_libs.cmake) and [src/server/detail/compressor.cc](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/src/server/detail/compressor.cc).

Dragonfly fetches and builds zstd 1.5.7 as a third-party library and links `TRDP::zstd` into its core library, per [helio/cmake/third_party.cmake](https://github.com/romange/helio/blob/master/cmake/third_party.cmake) and [src/core/CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/src/core/CMakeLists.txt).

Dragonfly's core CMake looks up the system `pcre2-8` library and links it in for regex/glob pattern matching (e.g. glob_matcher, KEYS-style patterns), per [src/core/CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/src/core/CMakeLists.txt).

Dragonfly's fiber/IO engine (helio, a git submodule of dragonfly) fetches and builds liburing 2.13 as a third-party dependency for its io_uring-based async I/O proactor, per [helio/cmake/third_party.cmake](https://github.com/romange/helio/blob/master/cmake/third_party.cmake).

Dragonfly's helio submodule fetches and builds xxHash 0.8.3 as a third-party hashing library, per [helio/cmake/third_party.cmake](https://github.com/romange/helio/blob/master/cmake/third_party.cmake).

Dragonfly builds a forked Lua 5.4.6a interpreter (dragonflydb/lua) as a third-party library and links `TRDP::lua` into its core for EVAL/FUNCTION scripting, per [src/external_libs.cmake](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/src/external_libs.cmake) and [src/core/CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/src/core/CMakeLists.txt).

RediSearch is a Redis module (loaded via `MODULE LOAD` / `--loadmodule`) that provides secondary indexing and full-text/vector search on top of Redis, and is meaningless without a running Redis server to host it — see the [RediSearch README](https://github.com/RediSearch/RediSearch/blob/master/README.md) ("RediSearch is a Redis module that provides querying, secondary indexing, and full-text search for Redis"; also noting that starting with Redis 8 it is built into Redis itself).

RediSearch vendors `redis/hiredis` as a git submodule (`deps/hiredis`, declared in [.gitmodules](https://github.com/RediSearch/RediSearch/blob/master/.gitmodules)) and builds/links it via `build/hiredis/hiredis.cmake` in the top-level [CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/RediSearch/RediSearch/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt), used by its cluster coordinator (`src/coord`) to speak RESP between shards.

The top-level [CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/RediSearch/RediSearch/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt) does `find_package(OpenSSL REQUIRED)` on macOS and links `crypto`/`ssl` (`SSL_LIBS`) on Linux, so RediSearch's coordinator/cluster networking is built against OpenSSL.

The build fails with a `FATAL_ERROR` unless `BOOST_DIR` resolves to a valid Boost installation (`include(${root}/build/boost/boost.cmake)` in [CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/RediSearch/RediSearch/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt)), making Boost a required external C++ build dependency; it is not one of the listed stack nodes.

RediSearch vendors `RedisAI/VectorSimilarity` as a git submodule (`deps/VectorSimilarity`, see [.gitmodules](https://github.com/RediSearch/RediSearch/blob/master/.gitmodules)), the engine that implements its KNN/vector similarity search feature; it is an external dependency not present in this stack's node list.

RedisJSON is implemented as a Redis module (its Cargo.toml pulls in the [redis-module](https://github.com/RedisLabsModules/redismodule-rs) crate) and must be loaded into a running Redis server to be usable, as its own [README](https://github.com/RedisJSON/RedisJSON) states: "RedisJSON is a Redis module that implements ECMA-404 ... as a native data type."

RedisJSON's [README](https://github.com/RedisJSON/RedisJSON) lists "Secondary index support when combined with RediSearch" as a primary feature, so indexing/querying JSON documents requires RediSearch to be loaded alongside it.

RedisBloom compiles to a loadable module ([redisbloom.so](https://github.com/RedisBloom/RedisBloom/blob/master/Dockerfile)) that is loaded into and run inside `redis-server` via `--loadmodule`, and as of Redis 8 its data structures are built into Redis itself, so it has no purpose without a Redis(-compatible) server host.

RedisTimeSeries is a loadable Redis module that only functions inside a running Redis server (loaded via `--loadmodule`), and its own README now states "[Starting with Redis 8, the Time Series data structure is integral to Redis](https://github.com/RedisTimeSeries/RedisTimeSeries#readme)" — confirming the module has no standalone existence apart from the Redis engine.

The repo's [`.install/install_redis.sh`](https://github.com/RedisTimeSeries/RedisTimeSeries/blob/master/.install/install_redis.sh) clones and builds `redis/redis` at a version pinned by `compatible_redis_version` in `pack/ramp.yml` in order to build and test the module against it, and `deps/RedisModulesSDK` (a git submodule per [`.gitmodules`](https://github.com/RedisTimeSeries/RedisTimeSeries/blob/master/.gitmodules)) provides the Redis Module API headers the C code links against.

The operator's go.mod requires github.com/redis/go-redis/v9 as its Redis client and its entire purpose is to provision and manage Redis standalone/cluster/replication/sentinel deployments, per the [README](https://github.com/OT-CONTAINER-KIT/redis-operator/blob/main/README.md).
go.mod pins k8s.io/client-go, k8s.io/apimachinery, k8s.io/api and sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime, since the operator is a Kubernetes controller that reconciles CRDs against the Kubernetes API server.

The operator injects and configures the oliver006/redis_exporter container as a sidecar (REDIS_EXPORTER_* env vars in internal/k8sutils/statefulset.go) to expose Redis metrics, as documented in the [Monitoring guide](https://ot-container-kit.github.io/redis-operator/guide/monitoring.html).

go.mod includes github.com/prometheus/client_golang and the operator sets prometheus.io/scrape and prometheus.io/port annotations for service discovery, so the metrics it exposes are only useful with a Prometheus (or ServiceMonitor-consuming) instance scraping them, per its [Monitoring docs](https://ot-container-kit.github.io/redis-operator/guide/monitoring.html).

The project's primary distribution and configuration mechanism is a Helm chart (values.yaml driving exporter/ServiceMonitor toggles), making Helm the practical way operators deploy and configure it, per the [Redis Operator introduction](https://ot-container-kit.github.io/redis-operator/guide/).

redis_exporter connects to and scrapes metrics from a running Redis instance to have anything to export, per the [README](https://github.com/oliver006/redis_exporter) ("Prometheus exporter for Valkey metrics (Redis-compatible)... Supports Valkey 7.x, 8.x, 9.x (and Redis)").

The exporter's README frames Valkey as its primary target ("Prometheus exporter for Valkey metrics (Redis-compatible)"), so a running Valkey instance is what it needs to scrape for [Valkey deployments](https://github.com/oliver006/redis_exporter).

redis_exporter exposes a `/metrics` (and `/scrape`) HTTP endpoint intended to be polled by a Prometheus server, as shown in the README's "Basic Prometheus Configuration" [scrape_configs example](https://github.com/oliver006/redis_exporter#basic-prometheus-configuration).

Memcached's Section 9 dependency table lists libevent as the mandatory event loop powering all network I/O, working fine on riscv64 via the Debian sid package with no known riscv64 issues (see [project-reports/memcached.md](https://github.com/memcached/memcached)).

OpenSSL is an optional dependency enabled via `--enable-tls` for TLS termination, and is flagged as the only dependency with meaningful riscv64-specific issues, including an AES constant-time gap on hardware lacking the Zkn extension ([OpenSSL #20980](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/20980), [#31080](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/31080)).
Lua 5.4 is vendored in-tree (`vendor/lua/`) as the scripting engine for the optional proxy subsystem (`--enable-proxy`), architecture-neutral C99 with a stale 5.4.3 copy versus upstream 5.4.7.

liburing is an optional vendored dependency fetched via `vendor/fetch.sh` for the experimental io_uring-based proxy async I/O path (`--enable-proxy-uring`), and upstream liburing carries an explicit riscv64 cross-compile CI entry.
The in-tree `xxhash.h` header implements request hash routing for the proxy subsystem and is architecture-neutral with no known riscv64 issues.
Memcached mandatorily depends on pthreads/glibc for threading and core runtime support, which is fully supported on riscv64 per the Debian riscv64 build.
Cyrus SASL / libsasl2 is an optional dependency for SASL authentication (`--enable-sasl`), a general C library with no riscv64 issues found and available as an Ubuntu/Debian riscv64 package.
libseccomp is an optional dependency for the syscall sandbox (`--enable-seccomp`, not enabled by default), supported on riscv64 since libseccomp v2.5.0 (2021).
mcmc is a vendored in-tree (`vendor/mcmc/`) internal client library used as the proxy subsystem's backend client, pure portable C with no riscv issues found.

mcrouter's [CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/facebook/mcrouter/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt) calls `find_package(OpenSSL REQUIRED)` and links `OpenSSL::SSL`/`OpenSSL::Crypto` (mcrouter advertises SSL support for client/server connections).
mcrouter's [CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/facebook/mcrouter/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt) calls `find_package(ZLIB REQUIRED)` and links `ZLIB::ZLIB` into the `mcrouter_deps` interface library.
mcrouter's [CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/facebook/mcrouter/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt) calls `find_package(LibEvent MODULE REQUIRED)` for its event loop / async I/O.

The [README](https://github.com/facebook/mcrouter#installing-from-source) states "Mcrouter depends on folly, wangle, fizz, and fbthrift", and CMakeLists.txt requires `find_package(folly CONFIG REQUIRED)` (plus wangle/fizz) as its core C++ async/networking foundation.

mcrouter's build requires `find_package(FBThrift CONFIG REQUIRED)` and generates its Memcache service RPC code (`MemcacheService.thrift`) via fbthrift codegen, per [CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/facebook/mcrouter/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt).

The [README](https://github.com/facebook/mcrouter) describes mcrouter as "a memcached protocol router for scaling memcached deployments" and its quick-start example routes requests to a running memcached instance, so it is useless without memcached servers behind it.

The [go.mod](https://github.com/prometheus/memcached_exporter/blob/master/go.mod) requires `github.com/prometheus/client_golang`, `github.com/prometheus/common`, and `github.com/prometheus/exporter-toolkit` to instrument metrics and serve the `/metrics` endpoint in Prometheus's exposition format.

Per the [README](https://github.com/prometheus/memcached_exporter#building), memcached_exporter connects to and scrapes stats from a running Memcached server (`--memcached.address`, default `localhost:11211`) — with no reachable Memcached instance it has nothing to export.

The [go.mod](https://github.com/prometheus/memcached_exporter/blob/master/go.mod) requires `github.com/grobie/gomemcache`, the Go memcached wire-protocol client used to query stats from the Memcached server being scraped.

containerd is the default CRI backend a Kubernetes cluster runs on top of, per [project-reports/kubernetes.md §9](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes) — riscv64 build/release artifacts exist but riscv64 integration-test CI is still open (containerd issues #13020/#13124).

runc is the low-level OCI runtime containerd invokes to actually start containers on a Kubernetes node, and its riscv64 CI/release artifacts already merged ([runc PR #5166](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/pull/5166)).

etcd is the control-plane key-value store a standard Kubernetes installation requires for cluster state, and the report identifies it as a hard riscv64 blocker since it ships no riscv64 release binaries in any current series.

kubernetes/kubernetes's go.mod directly requires `google.golang.org/protobuf` (plus vendored `gogo/protobuf`/`golang/protobuf`), which backs the protobuf wire codec that k8s.io/apimachinery uses for internal API-server-to-component serialization, verified directly in the repo's [go.mod](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/go.mod).

Kubernetes vendors `github.com/prometheus/client_golang` — directly imported some 30+ times under `staging/src/k8s.io/component-base` — to instrument and expose every core component's `/metrics` endpoint in Prometheus text format, per a live GitHub code search of [kubernetes/kubernetes](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes).

kube-apiserver and kubelet directly depend on the OpenTelemetry Go SDK's OTLP gRPC exporter (go.opentelemetry.io/otel, a direct go.mod dependency) to emit distributed traces, a feature that only becomes useful once an OpenTelemetry Collector (or OTLP-compatible backend) is deployed to receive and route those spans, per [Traces For Kubernetes System Components](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/system-traces/).

Pod networking (bridge, loopback, host-local, portmap) requires the standard CNI plugin binaries, which per the report already ship riscv64 release artifacts (`cni-plugins-linux-riscv64-v1.9.1.tgz`) with no open blocking issues.
CoreDNS is the default cluster DNS addon a functioning cluster deploys, and per the report already ships riscv64 release artifacts (`coredns_1.14.4_linux_riscv64.tgz`) with no open blocking issues.

Pod live migration and checkpoint/restore functionality depends on CRIU, which per the report has had no riscv64 implementation since an issue opened in 2021 ([criu#1702](https://github.com/checkpoint-restore/criu/issues/1702)), blocking that feature entirely on riscv64.

containerd relies on [opencontainers/runc](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc) as the OCI runtime that performs the actual container exec, namespace, and cgroup operations, per project-reports/containerd.md §9.

containerd uses checkpoint-restore/criu (via go-criu) to implement checkpoint/restore in userspace, a feature that remains incomplete on riscv64 per [criu issue #1702](https://github.com/checkpoint-restore/criu/issues/1702).
containerd uses the klauspost/compress library for zstd, S2, and gzip compression of OCI image layers, with no riscv64 SIMD path so it falls back to generic Go.
containerd uses its own containerd/cgroups library for cgroups v1/v2 management on Linux.
containerd uses containernetworking/plugins to provide CNI network plugin support for container networking.
containerd uses google.golang.org/grpc as the transport for its CRI, NRI, and ttrpc APIs.
containerd embeds go.etcd.io/bbolt as the on-disk key-value store backing its metadata database.
containerd uses the go.opentelemetry.io/otel Go SDK for its distributed-tracing instrumentation.
containerd relies on golang.org/x/sys for Linux syscall bindings, including the full riscv64 syscall tables and RISCVHWProbe wrapper.
containerd uses erofs/go-erofs to support EROFS as a read-only snapshotter filesystem, though this path is untested on riscv64.
containerd implements the Kubernetes CRI interface defined by the k8s.io/cri-api and cri-client Go modules published from the Kubernetes project.
containerd uses google.golang.org/protobuf for Protocol Buffers serialization across its API and CRI surface.
containerd uses Microsoft/hcsshim as its Windows Host Compute Service shim, a Windows-only dependency not compiled on Linux/riscv64.

containerd's built-in `io.containerd.tracing.processor.v1.otlp` plugin exports traces via OTLP to an endpoint, so a running OpenTelemetry Collector (or compatible receiver) is needed for containerd's distributed tracing to actually be useful, per [containerd docs/tracing.md](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/main/docs/tracing.md).

runc links libseccomp (v2.6.0) via CGo for syscall filtering, and it must be cross-built from source (`./configure --host riscv64-linux-gnu`) for riscv64 per [project-reports/runc.md](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc) Section 5/9.

runc links libpathrs (cyphar.com/go-pathrs v0.2.5, Rust) via CGo for safe path resolution using `openat2`, cross-built with cargo targeting riscv64gc-unknown-linux-gnu per project-reports/runc.md Section 5/9.

runc's optional checkpoint/restore feature depends on the checkpoint-restore/go-criu bindings and the external CRIU C library, whose riscv64 CI build is blocked on a missing libnftables-dev package ([CRIU issue #2714](https://github.com/checkpoint-restore/criu/issues/2714)) per project-reports/runc.md Section 9.
etcd depends on google.golang.org/protobuf (v1.36.11) for gRPC wire serialization, a pure-Go dependency with no riscv64 build issues per the [project report](project-reports/etcd.md).

etcd vendors github.com/cespare/xxhash/v2 (v2.3.0) for fast 64-bit hashing used by the Prometheus metrics client, falling back to a pure-Go path on riscv64 per the [project report](project-reports/etcd.md).
etcd links github.com/prometheus/client_golang (v1.23.2) to expose its metrics endpoint, per the [project report](project-reports/etcd.md).

etcd's distributed-tracing feature exports OTLP spans to a collector endpoint (`--distributed-tracing-address`, default `localhost:4317`), so a running [OpenTelemetry Collector](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.5/op-guide/monitoring/) is needed to actually receive/use the traces.

Helm's [go.mod](https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/main/go.mod) directly requires k8s.io/client-go, k8s.io/apimachinery, k8s.io/apiserver, k8s.io/cli-runtime and k8s.io/kubectl, and Helm's entire purpose (installing/upgrading/templating charts) is to manage resources on a running Kubernetes cluster.

Helm's go.mod directly requires github.com/lib/pq, github.com/jmoiron/sqlx, github.com/Masterminds/squirrel and github.com/rubenv/sql-migrate to implement its optional SQL release-storage driver ([sql.go](https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/main/pkg/storage/driver/sql.go)), and Helm's docs state that with `HELM_DRIVER=sql` "only PostgreSQL is supported at this moment" ([Permissions management for SQL storage backend](https://helm.sh/docs/topics/permissions_sql_storage_backend/)).

k0s statically embeds the full Kubernetes control plane (kubelet, kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler) at version 1.36.1 as its core orchestration engine ([k0s report §9](https://github.com/k0sproject/k0s)).
k0s embeds containerd 2.3.2 as its CRI container runtime.
k0s embeds runc 1.4.3 as the low-level OCI runtime invoked by containerd.
k0s embeds etcd 3.7.0-rc.0 as the distributed key-value store backing multi-node HA control-plane state (multi-node HA is not achievable without it).
k0s bundles Helm v3.21.1 as its Kubernetes package manager for chart-based application installs.
k0s is written entirely in Go (1.26.4 toolchain, no C/assembly) and requires it to compile the single static binary.
k0s embeds kine 0.16.2, a lightweight SQLite/Postgres/MySQL-backed etcd-API shim used as a single-node alternative to etcd.
kine (and transitively k0s) uses the pure-Go modernc.org/sqlite v1.52.0 library as its embedded datastore driver.
k0s embeds konnectivity 0.36.0 as the network proxy connecting the control plane to worker nodes.
k0s embeds iptables 1.8.13 for the packet filtering its CNI networking requires.
k0s embeds keepalived 2.3.4 to provide VRRP-based virtual IP failover for HA control-plane setups.
k0s links golang.org/x/crypto for TLS/crypto functionality.
k0s bundles kube-router as its default CNI plugin providing pod networking.
k0s supports Calico as an alternative, optional CNI plugin in place of kube-router.
k0s's Node-Local Load Balancing (NLLB) enterprise feature indirectly depends on Envoy as its embedded L4/L7 proxy image.
k0s's Kubernetes conformance-testing pipeline depends on sonobuoy v0.57.3 to run conformance test suites.
k0s bundles CoreDNS as the default cluster DNS server image; the cluster has non-functional DNS without it.
k0s's release process indirectly depends on anchore/syft for SBOM generation.
k3s embeds a fork of k3s-io/kubernetes (v1.36.2-k3s1) as its control plane and kubelet, per [k3s.md Section 9](project-reports/k3s.md).
k3s bundles a containerd fork (v2.3.1-k3s2) as its default Container Runtime Interface implementation, per [k3s.md Section 9](project-reports/k3s.md).
k3s uses opencontainers/runc (v1.4.2) as the low-level OCI container runtime beneath containerd, per [k3s.md Section 9](project-reports/k3s.md).
k3s embeds a fork of etcd (v3.6.12-k3s1) as an optional/embedded key-value store for cluster state, per [k3s.md Section 9](project-reports/k3s.md).
k3s's helm-controller relies on Helm (v3.14.0+) to reconcile the built-in HelmChart CRD, per [k3s.md Section 9](project-reports/k3s.md).
OpenSSL is used via CGO for TLS and crypto primitives inside k3s's bundled containerd/runc, per [k3s.md Section 9](project-reports/k3s.md).
k3s uses its k3s-io/kine (v0.16.1) fork as an etcd-API shim allowing SQLite/Postgres/MySQL to back the datastore instead of etcd, per [k3s.md Section 9](project-reports/k3s.md).
flannel-io/flannel (v0.28.4) is k3s's default CNI network backend (VXLAN/WireGuard), per [k3s.md Section 9](project-reports/k3s.md).
containernetworking/plugins (v1.9.1) supplies the bridge, loopback, and portmap CNI plugins k3s ships, per [k3s.md Section 9](project-reports/k3s.md).
coredns/coredns is bundled as k3s's default in-cluster DNS addon, per [k3s.md Section 9](project-reports/k3s.md).
traefik/traefik is k3s's default ingress controller and reverse proxy, per [k3s.md Section 9](project-reports/k3s.md).

The project report's Dependencies section documents `cespare/xxhash/v2` (an xxHash implementation) as the 64-bit hash Prometheus uses for TSDB chunk indexing and label fingerprinting, falling back to a pure-Go implementation on riscv64 instead of the asm paths used on amd64/arm64.

The report lists `golang/snappy` and the Snappy component of `klauspost/compress` as implementing the Snappy compression format for the legacy remote-write protocol and TSDB, both compiling as pure Go on riscv64.

The report lists the zstd component of `klauspost/compress` as used for remote-write payload compression, noting it has no riscv64 SIMD acceleration (only AVX2/NEON on amd64/arm64) and runs the pure-Go codec there.

The report's Dependencies section treats the Go toolchain (compiler, GC, scheduler, stdlib, crypto) as Prometheus's foundational build/runtime dependency, noting riscv64 is a secondary Go port with open toolchain issues such as [golang/go#74683](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/74683).

The report documents `golang.org/x/crypto` as providing TLS/AEAD/certificate handling for HTTPS scraping and remote-write, falling back to pure-Go on riscv64 (no AES-GCM/ChaCha20 asm) for roughly 3-5x slower TLS throughput than amd64/arm64.

The report lists `prometheus/procfs` as reading `/proc` and `/sys` for node metrics, with riscv64 CPUInfo parsing added in [procfs PR #318](https://github.com/prometheus/procfs/pull/318) and a dispatch-wiring bug fixed in [PR #325](https://github.com/prometheus/procfs/pull/325).

The report documents `prometheus/client_golang` as the library Prometheus uses for its own self-instrumentation, noting it was previously broken on riscv64 until its procfs dependency was bumped ([PR #833](https://github.com/prometheus/client_golang/pull/833)).
The report lists `google/pprof` as powering CPU/memory profiling and the `/debug/pprof` endpoint, building cleanly on riscv64 via standard Go runtime stack walking.
The report documents `edsrzf/mmap-go` as providing the memory-mapped file I/O used for the TSDB write-ahead log and chunk files, arch-independent via `golang.org/x/sys`.
The report lists `grafana/regexp`, a pure-Go fork of stdlib regexp, as the DFA-based regex engine used for PromQL label selector matching.
The report documents `google.golang.org/grpc` as the transport used for Prometheus's remote-write protocol, with no architecture-specific code.
The report lists `go.uber.org/automaxprocs` as setting GOMAXPROCS from the cgroup CPU quota, a pure-Go dependency with no riscv64 issues.
The report documents `KimMachineGun/automemlimit` as deriving a soft memory limit from the cgroup `memory.max` value, a pure-Go dependency.
The report lists `dennwc/varint` as the varint-encoding library used for TSDB posting lists, a pure-Go dependency with no riscv64 issues.

node_exporter's [go.mod](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prometheus/node_exporter/master/go.mod) directly imports the Prometheus project's own libraries (prometheus/client_golang, client_model, common, exporter-toolkit) to implement its /metrics HTTP endpoint in the Prometheus exposition format.

node_exporter is described as a ["Prometheus exporter for hardware and OS metrics"](https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter) whose whole purpose is to be scraped by a Prometheus (or Prometheus-compatible) server -- without one polling its /metrics endpoint it produces no useful monitoring outcome.

The collector's Go-based dependency table lists `google.golang.org/protobuf` v1.36.11 as providing OTLP wire serialization, built as pure Go and statically linked ([project-reports/opentelemetry.md](project-reports/opentelemetry.md), Section 9).

glibc is listed as the system C library required for CGo and native linking, functional on riscv64 since glibc 2.27, with deployments on glibc <2.42 noted to carry crash-class bugs ([project-reports/opentelemetry.md](project-reports/opentelemetry.md), Section 9).

The Go compiler/runtime is documented as the build toolchain and runtime for all Go components, statically linked into collector binaries via Go module distribution ([project-reports/opentelemetry.md](project-reports/opentelemetry.md), Section 9).

`google.golang.org/grpc` is documented as providing the OTLP gRPC export transport, built as pure Go and statically linked into the collector ([project-reports/opentelemetry.md](project-reports/opentelemetry.md), Section 9).

The official core `otelcol` distribution bundles the Prometheus receiver, exporter, and remote-write exporter as first-class components, so scraping or exporting Prometheus-format metrics needs a Prometheus-compatible target/server present to be useful ([opentelemetry-collector-releases otelcol manifest.yaml](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/blob/main/distributions/otelcol/manifest.yaml), [Prometheus and OpenTelemetry - Better Together](https://opentelemetry.io/blog/2024/prom-and-otel/)).

Grafana's [go.mod](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/go.mod) lists `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5` as a direct dependency, used both as the core PostgreSQL datasource driver and for Grafana's own Postgres-backed database/unified storage.
`github.com/jackc/pgx/v5` is a direct entry in Grafana's [go.mod](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/go.mod), the pgx driver package used for PostgreSQL connectivity.

Grafana's [go.mod](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/go.mod) depends directly on `github.com/go-sql-driver/mysql`, powering both the core MySQL datasource plugin and MySQL as a backend database option.
`github.com/go-sql-driver/mysql` v1.10.0 is a direct dependency in Grafana's [go.mod](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/go.mod).

Grafana depends directly on `github.com/redis/go-redis/v9` ([go.mod](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/go.mod)) and its docs describe configuring Redis as the `[remote_cache]` backend and the `ha_engine` for [Grafana Live high availability](https://community.grafana.com/t/remote-cache-for-grafana-sessions/77076).

Grafana's [go.mod](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/go.mod) directly depends on `github.com/bradfitz/gomemcache` and `github.com/grafana/gomemcache`, used to support Memcached as an alternative `[remote_cache]` backend.

`github.com/pgvector/pgvector-go` is a direct dependency in Grafana's [go.mod](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/go.mod), used for vector-search/AI features backed by pgvector in PostgreSQL.

Grafana's [go.mod](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/go.mod) directly depends on `github.com/prometheus/prometheus` (embedding PromQL/rules code for unified alerting) as well as `github.com/prometheus/client_golang` and `github.com/prometheus/alertmanager`.

Grafana's [go.mod](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/go.mod) directly depends on `k8s.io/apiserver`, `k8s.io/client-go`, `k8s.io/api` and related packages, which implement Grafana's Kubernetes-style aggregated API server (App Platform).

Grafana's [go.mod](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/go.mod) directly depends on `google.golang.org/protobuf`, `github.com/golang/protobuf`, and `github.com/gogo/protobuf` for its gRPC/protobuf-based APIs.
`github.com/cespare/xxhash/v2` is a direct dependency in Grafana's [go.mod](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/go.mod).
`github.com/golang/snappy` is a direct dependency in Grafana's [go.mod](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/go.mod), used for Snappy compression (e.g. Prometheus remote-write payloads).

Grafana directly depends on `go.opentelemetry.io/collector/pdata` ([go.mod](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/go.mod)), the OpenTelemetry Collector's data-model package, for handling OTLP telemetry data.

Grafana Alloy is described on its own GitHub repo as an "[OpenTelemetry Collector distribution](https://github.com/grafana/alloy) with programmable pipelines" and bundles upstream OpenTelemetry Collector components generated from an OpenTelemetry Collector Builder (OCB) manifest.

Per project-reports/grafana-alloy.md Section 9, Alloy vendors prometheus/prometheus as its core metrics scraping engine, TSDB, and PromQL implementation, building on riscv64 with no open correctness bugs noted.

Alloy's [prometheus.remote_write](https://grafana.com/docs/alloy/latest/reference/components/prometheus/prometheus.remote_write/) component forwards scraped metrics over the network to a Prometheus-compatible remote-write endpoint, so a running Prometheus (or compatible receiver) is needed for the metrics pipeline to be useful.
Per project-reports/grafana-alloy.md Section 9, Alloy embeds prometheus/node_exporter to collect host hardware and OS metrics via the prometheus.exporter.unix component.

Per project-reports/grafana-alloy.md Section 9, Alloy uses cespare/xxhash/v2 (xxHash-64) for metric label fingerprinting, falling back to a pure-Go path on architectures without hand-written assembly such as riscv64.

The [Grafana Alloy homepage](https://grafana.com/oss/alloy/) states it sends collected telemetry to "the Grafana LGTM stack, or Grafana Cloud" for storage and visualization, though Alloy's own collection pipelines can run without Grafana present.

Per project-reports/grafana-alloy.md Section 9, Alloy (~97% Go) depends on the Go toolchain/runtime for compilation, GC, and stdlib, and three open riscv64 Go runtime bugs (including a memory-corruption miscompile) are flagged as blocking for production riscv64 use.

Per project-reports/grafana-alloy.md Section 9, the loki.source.journal component uses coreos/go-systemd to read the systemd journal via libsystemd through CGO, compiling to a no-op stub when the promtail_journal_enabled build tag is absent.
Per project-reports/grafana-alloy.md Section 9, Alloy vendors grafana/beyla for eBPF-based HTTP/gRPC auto-instrumentation, which Beyla's own Makefile hardcodes to linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 only.

Per project-reports/grafana-alloy.md Section 9, the pyroscope.ebpf component vendors go.opentelemetry.io/ebpf-profiler for continuous eBPF CPU profiling, whose README states only amd64 and arm64 are supported.
Per project-reports/grafana-alloy.md Section 9, Alloy uses klauspost/compress for zstd, gzip, and S2/Snappy compression of OTel spans, remote-write payloads, and the WAL.
Per project-reports/grafana-alloy.md Section 9, Alloy vendors google/cadvisor for container resource metrics collection in Kubernetes environments.

Per project-reports/grafana-alloy.md Section 9, Alloy uses golang.org/x/crypto for TLS primitives (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305), falling back to a pure-Go implementation with no riscv64 assembly acceleration.
Per project-reports/grafana-alloy.md Section 9, Alloy uses google/pprof for CPU/memory profiling and flamegraph generation.
Per project-reports/grafana-alloy.md Section 9, Alloy's loki.write component forwards logs to grafana/loki for ingestion and storage; Loki builds for riscv64 with release artifacts available.

Per project-reports/grafana-alloy.md Section 9, Alloy's pyroscope.write component forwards continuous-profiling data to grafana/pyroscope, which builds in pure-Go mode on riscv64 though its eBPF profiling mode shares the same architecture limitations as ebpf-profiler.
Per project-reports/grafana-alloy.md Section 9, Alloy uses KimMachineGun/automemlimit to map the cgroup memory.max limit to a Go soft memory limit.
Per project-reports/grafana-alloy.md Section 9, Alloy vendors grafana/dskit, a shared infrastructure toolkit providing the consistent-hash ring, memberlist, and gRPC helpers used for clustering.
Per project-reports/grafana-alloy.md Section 9, Alloy uses IBM/sarama as its Kafka client library for Kafka-related components.

The [OpenSSL report](https://github.com/openssl/openssl) documents glibc as OpenSSL's runtime C library, notably providing the `riscv_hwprobe` syscall used for RISC-V ISA capability detection, with build/release green and mostly-green tests (a fixed SIGILL in `__memset_vector` when RVV is disabled).
Section 9 of the OpenSSL report lists zlib as an optional dependency used for TLS compression, green across riscv64 build/test/release.

Section 9 lists zstd as an optional dependency for certificate compression, mostly green on riscv64 aside from an open upstream [zstd issue](https://github.com/facebook/zstd/issues/4622) affecting decompression throughput, not correctness.
Section 9 documents Perl 5 plus the Text::Template module as a build-only dependency, used to generate the perlasm-based RISC-V crypto assembly, and reports it green across build/test/release.
Section 9 documents the GNU assembler (binutils) as required to assemble all perlasm-generated crypto `.S` files, needing version >= 2.38 for the Zvk vector-crypto instruction encodings.
Section 9 lists brotli as an optional dependency for TLS certificate compression, green across riscv64 build/test/release.

Section 9 lists musl libc as an alternative runtime C library that is broken for OpenSSL's riscv64 ISA feature detection, per [Issue #28118](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/28118), causing accelerated code paths to silently fall back to generic C.

BoringSSL vendors Google Test (`third_party/googletest`) as its unit-test framework; it builds and mostly passes on riscv64 except for `GetThreadCountTest.ReturnsCorrectValue`, which fails per [googletest issue #3756](https://github.com/google/googletest/issues/3756).
BoringSSL vendors Google's `benchmark` library (`third_party/benchmark`) as the microbenchmark harness for its performance tests, which builds and runs on riscv64 with no known blocking issues.

BoringSSL vendors fiat-crypto's formally-verified finite-field arithmetic (`third_party/fiat`), and riscv64 relies entirely on its generic C paths (`curve25519_64.h`, `p256_64.h`) since no riscv64 assembly backend exists.
BoringSSL vendors Google's Wycheproof known-answer test vectors (`third_party/wycheproof_testvectors`) as static JSON data with no architecture-specific dependency.

BoringSSL optionally links libunwind for stack unwinding in sanitizer/profiling builds on non-Android systems, but this is not a riscv64 blocker since BoringSSL otherwise builds with `-fno-exceptions -fno-rtti`.
BoringSSL depends on POSIX threading/synchronization primitives, which ship in glibc (and musl) for riscv64 Linux with no known issues per the report's dependency table.
BoringSSL's Go-based build tooling (the `delocate` and `inject_hash` utilities, not the C library runtime) uses the pure-Go `golang.org/x/crypto` module, which has no riscv64 issues.
BoringSSL's Go build tooling uses the pure-Go `filippo.io/edwards25519` module for Edwards-curve arithmetic in its build scripts, with no riscv64 issues.

zlib documents no external library dependencies beyond the C standard library, listing libc (glibc) as its C runtime dependency for both build and runtime on riscv64 with no blockers (project-reports/zlib.md, Section 9).
LZ4 vendors an old xxHash v0.6.5 snapshot (`lib/xxhash.c`) for content checksums in the lz4frame streaming format, as documented in [project-reports/lz4.md Section 9](https://github.com/lz4/lz4).

LZ4's only external runtime dependency is the C standard library (memcpy/memmove etc.), which is mature and fully tested on riscv64 via QEMU CI per [project-reports/lz4.md Section 9](https://github.com/lz4/lz4).

LZ4 optionally supports CMake as an alternative build system (`build/cmake/CMakeLists.txt`) alongside its primary Makefile, a build-time-only dependency per [project-reports/lz4.md Section 9](https://github.com/lz4/lz4).
zstd's optional multithreading support (`ZSTD_MULTITHREAD_SUPPORT`) links pthreads, which is part of glibc, per [project-reports/zstd.md §9](https://github.com/facebook/zstd).
zstd bundles a vanilla-C copy of xxhash (XXH32/XXH64) as `lib/common/xxhash.c` for content checksums, per [project-reports/zstd.md §9](https://github.com/facebook/zstd/blob/dev/lib/common/xxhash.c).

zlib is an optional dependency enabling zstd's `zlibWrapper` drop-in-replacement mode, confirmed by the `ZSTD_ZLIB_SUPPORT`/`find_package(ZLIB REQUIRED)` option in [build/cmake/programs/CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/facebook/zstd/blob/dev/build/cmake/programs/CMakeLists.txt).

LZ4 is an optional dependency used for zlibWrapper parity and appears in the CLI's contrib build targets, confirmed by the `ZSTD_LZ4_SUPPORT`/`find_package(LibLZ4 REQUIRED)` option in [build/cmake/programs/CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/facebook/zstd/blob/dev/build/cmake/programs/CMakeLists.txt).

liblzma/xz-utils is an optional dependency enabling legacy `.xz`/`.lzma` stream support via `-DZSTD_LZMA_SUPPORT=ON`, confirmed by `find_package(LibLZMA REQUIRED)` in [build/cmake/programs/CMakeLists.txt](https://github.com/facebook/zstd/blob/dev/build/cmake/programs/CMakeLists.txt).

Snappy's benchmark suite optionally links zlib as a comparison codec (`HAVE_LIBZ`), and this is not a runtime dependency of the library itself, per [project-reports/snappy.md §9](project-reports/snappy.md).

Snappy's benchmark suite optionally links LZ4 as a comparison codec (`HAVE_LIBLZ4`), which is not a runtime dependency of the library itself, per [project-reports/snappy.md §9](project-reports/snappy.md).

Snappy's benchmark suite optionally links LZO2 as a comparison codec (`HAVE_LIBLZO2`), which is not a runtime dependency of the library itself, per [project-reports/snappy.md §9](project-reports/snappy.md).
Snappy vendors google/benchmark as a git submodule (`third_party/benchmark`) to build its benchmark framework, per [project-reports/snappy.md §9](project-reports/snappy.md).
Snappy vendors google/googletest as a git submodule (`third_party/googletest`) to build and run its unit test suite, per [project-reports/snappy.md §9](project-reports/snappy.md).

jemalloc requires glibc-provided pthreads for TLS/mutex/background-thread management, libm for log(3) when heap profiling is enabled, and libdl for dlsym()-based lazy-lock multithread detection, per [project-reports/jemalloc.md Section 9](project-reports/jemalloc.md).

On riscv64 jemalloc requires the GCC runtime libatomic to emulate 8/16-bit compare-exchange operations the RISC-V A extension doesn't provide natively, auto-linked via the -pthread flag since [PR #1402](https://github.com/jemalloc/jemalloc/pull/1402).
jemalloc optionally links libunwind for backtrace support in heap profiling when built with --enable-prof-libunwind, per project-reports/jemalloc.md Section 9.
jemalloc optionally uses libgcc_s's _Unwind_Backtrace for heap profiling when built with --enable-prof-libgcc, per project-reports/jemalloc.md Section 9.
jemalloc optionally links libstdc++ to provide C++ operator new/delete integration when built with --enable-cxx (default on), per project-reports/jemalloc.md Section 9.

Section 9 lists protobuf as a critical first-order dependency used for profile proto serialization and the profile builder, with no official riscv64 protoc binary shipped ([protobuf#12266](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/12266)).

Section 9 documents glibc as a dependency via its rseq per-thread registration (glibc 2.35+), which conflicts with tcmalloc's own rseq registration and is tracked as [tcmalloc issue #144](https://github.com/google/tcmalloc/issues/144).

Section 9 lists abseil-cpp as tcmalloc's primary load-bearing dependency, providing logging, synchronization, CRC, hash tables, stack traces, cycle clock, and string utilities, with an open riscv64 sampler segfault ([abseil-cpp#2002](https://github.com/abseil/abseil-cpp/issues/2002)).

PCRE2's pcre2grep utility optionally links zlib to support scanning gzip-compressed input, and this builds fine on riscv64 (Debian sid ships zlib1g for riscv64) per [project-reports/pcre2.md §9](project-reports/pcre2.md).

PCRE2's JIT engine requires pthreads (part of glibc) for memory allocation on Linux when JIT is enabled, fully supported on riscv64 via glibc 2.27+ per [project-reports/pcre2.md §9](project-reports/pcre2.md).
pcre2grep optionally links bzip2 to support scanning bzip2-compressed input, building fine on riscv64 per [project-reports/pcre2.md §9](project-reports/pcre2.md).
pcre2test optionally links libreadline for interactive input line editing, with no riscv64-specific gaps per [project-reports/pcre2.md §9](project-reports/pcre2.md).
libedit is documented as a portable drop-in alternative to libreadline for pcre2test's interactive input, with no riscv64-specific issues per [project-reports/pcre2.md §9](project-reports/pcre2.md).

Valgrind is used for memory debugging during PCRE2's build/test process (not an end-user runtime dependency), with riscv64 (RV64GC) support added in Valgrind 3.25.0 per [project-reports/pcre2.md §9](project-reports/pcre2.md).

SLJIT is the embedded JIT backend, vendored directly under deps/sljit, that generates native machine code at runtime for PCRE2's regex match loop, and is the critical dependency actively maintained for riscv64 per [project-reports/pcre2.md §9](project-reports/pcre2.md).

ICU4C relies on glibc (libc, libpthread, libm, libdl) for POSIX threading, locale support such as nl_langinfo, math functions, and dynamic loading, per [project-reports/icu.md Section 9](https://github.com/unicode-org/icu).
ICU's optional icu-le-hb paragraph-layout engine (--enable-layoutex, disabled by default) links against HarfBuzz, which is itself built and installed on riscv64 in Debian.
ICU4C vendors a bundled copy of Google's double-conversion library under vendor/double-conversion/ for float-to-string and string-to-float conversion.
ICU4C requires C++17 and links against the libstdc++6 and libgcc-s1 runtime libraries provided by the GCC riscv64 toolchain.
ICU4J is pure Java with no JNI, so it requires a JVM at runtime; OpenJDK's riscv64 port (JEP 422) is available in Fedora and Debian.
ICU4J's build and JMH-based benchmarking are driven by Maven, an architecture-agnostic build-time dependency not needed for ICU4C.
libevent's bufferevent_openssl layer uses [OpenSSL](https://www.openssl.org/) as an optional TLS backend, and it is the only libevent dependency carrying RISC-V-specific assembly (Zkn, Zvk, RVV).
libevent's bufferevent_mbedtls layer offers Mbed TLS as an alternative, optional TLS backend to OpenSSL.
zlib is used only by libevent's test suite for compression testing, not linked into the production library.
libevent's evthread_use_pthreads locking relies on glibc's pthreads implementation and is required for thread-safety on Linux.

liburing is a userspace wrapper over the Linux kernel's io_uring syscalls (io_uring_setup, io_uring_enter, io_uring_register), confirmed by [PR #928/#930 riscv64 port](https://github.com/axboe/liburing/pull/930) and the [README](https://github.com/axboe/liburing/blob/master/README).
Building liburing requires Linux UAPI headers (linux/io_uring.h, linux/fs.h, linux/time_types.h), with compat.h providing fallbacks for missing symbols across kernel versions.

libbpf is an optional dependency required only to enable io_uring_bpf BPF-filter support, verified in liburing's [configure script](https://github.com/axboe/liburing/blob/master/configure) which probes for a BPF toolchain.

liburing's CI cross-compiles riscv64 using the gcc-riscv64-linux-gnu toolchain via a custom ./configure script, per [.github/workflows/ci.yml](https://github.com/axboe/liburing/blob/master/.github/workflows/ci.yml).

liburing optionally builds in a freestanding nolibc mode (CONFIG_NOLIBC=y) that eliminates the libc dependency entirely, supported on riscv64 since liburing-2.5 with an added -lgcc to fix a __clzdi2 linker error.

libnuma uses glibc (or musl) as its C runtime for syscall(), sched_setaffinity(), and sched_getaffinity(), guarded by a __GLIBC_PREREQ(2,11) check that riscv64 always satisfies, per [project-reports/libnuma.md §9](https://github.com/numactl/numactl).

The Ubuntu/Debian `libprotobuf-dev` package declares a direct dependency on `zlib1g-dev` in the project graph.; Section 9 of the [project report](project-reports/protocol-buffers.md) lists zlib 1.3.1 as an optional dependency used for wire-format message compression, building cleanly on riscv64 with no SIMD.

Section 9 documents abseil-cpp as the core C++ foundation (strings, hashing, containers, CRC32C, synchronization, logging) directly linked into libprotobuf, and calls it out as the most likely source of riscv64 build failures (missing `-latomic`).
Section 9 lists re2 2024-07-02 as used for regex matching in protoc option parsing and TextFormat, with no riscv64-specific issues noted.

Section 9 lists googletest 1.17.0 as a test-only dependency, with a known upstream gtest self-test failure on riscv64 ([googletest#3756](https://github.com/google/googletest/issues/3756)) that does not affect protobuf's own tests.
Section 9 lists jsoncpp 1.9.6 as used by the conformance test runner and the TextFormat JSON codec, with no riscv64-specific issues.
Section 9 lists utf8_range (bundled in-tree under third_party/) as providing UTF-8 validation for string fields; it is pure portable C on riscv64 with no SIMD/RVV path.

The Ubuntu `lua5.4` CLI package formally depends on libreadline for interactive line-editing/history, and Lua's own source ([lua.c](https://github.com/lua/lua/blob/master/lua.c)) supports linking against or dynamically loading `readline`/`add_history` when built with `LUA_USE_READLINE`, though it falls back to a built-in line reader without it.

glibc requires GCC 12.1+ as its primary riscv64 compiler (enforced at configure time), with GCC 15+ mandatory when building with RVV support, per [project-reports/glibc.md §9](project-reports/glibc.md).
glibc needs GNU binutils 2.39+ for its assembler/linker, since R_RISCV_ALIGN and R_RISCV_RELATIVE relocation support are required for static PIE on riscv64.
glibc's build requires Linux kernel headers 3.2+ (via --with-headers) to define the riscv64 syscall ABI it wraps.
glibc's test infrastructure scripts require Python 3.4+ to run.
glibc's test suite relies on GDB 7.8+ for pretty-printer testing.
glibc's test/debug tooling uses elfutils (eu-readelf) as part of its static PIE probe.
libffi is a runtime dependency of the Python interpreter that glibc's own test scripts run under.
glibc's memusagestat tool optionally links libgd, which in turn depends on zlib, per [project-reports/glibc.md §9](project-reports/glibc.md).
glibc's memusagestat tool optionally links libgd, which in turn depends on libpng for image output.
glibc's nscd daemon optionally uses libcap for SELinux capability support.
glibc's nscd daemon optionally links libselinux for SELinux policy support.
glibc's nscd daemon optionally links libaudit for SELinux audit logging.
glibc's build orchestration requires GNU make 4.0+.
glibc's test harness requires GNU awk (gawk) 3.1.2+ built with MPFR support.
glibc's build requires GNU bison 2.7+ for parser generation.

libmvec ships inside the glibc tree and links against glibc's libm at build time, per `mathvec/Depend` which lists only `math` — see [libmvec.md §9](project-reports/libmvec.md) and the [glibc source repository](https://sourceware.org/git/glibc.git).

Any RVV-using libmvec build is hard-gated by `sysdeps/riscv/preconfigure.ac` to require GCC >= 15, and the proposed GCC SIMD-clone target hooks (needed to auto-generate `_ZGV*` symbols) remain an unmerged RFC as of April 2026 ([gcc-patches/714883](https://gcc.gnu.org/pipermail/gcc-patches/2026-April/714883.html)).
libmvec's build requires GNU binutils >= 2.39 for RVV instruction support and linker relaxation (R_RISCV_ALIGN), per libmvec.md Section 9.
A future RVV-enabled libmvec depends on kernel support for the `RISCV_HWPROBE_IMA_V` probe (Linux 6.4+) to detect vector-extension availability at runtime, per libmvec.md Section 9.

libmvec's vector-function symbol naming scheme (`_ZGVr<lmul><mask><len><params>_<func>`) depends on the RISC-V psABI vector name-mangling specification, resolved via [riscv-elf-psabi-doc PR #455](https://github.com/riscv-non-isa/riscv-elf-psabi-doc/pull/455) merged June 18, 2026.
The proposed RISC-V libmvec implementations are derived from Rivos's [veclibm](https://github.com/rivosinc/veclibm) reference library, now MIT-licensed and archived, per libmvec.md Section 9.

Clang's auto-vectorizer needs a vector-library mapping to call libmvec's `_ZGV*` symbols, proposed but still a WIP/Draft with failing tests in [LLVM PR #193721](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/193721).
